name: aspirecures-weekly-research
description: Weekly research pipeline for AspireCURES: collect candidates from Europe PMC/PubMed/ClinicalTrials.gov/ISRCTN, Claude-gate each against strict page relevance rules, emit a JSON report consumed by the commit agent which renders + validates + commits disease pages (two-agent split)
schedule_human: Weekly Monday at 9:17 AM ET (13:17 UTC, matching CI workflow)

preparer.description: Collects from Europe PMC + PubMed + ClinicalTrials.gov + ISRCTN, applies Claude curation gate (strict relevance + credibility + patient-appropriateness + confidence threshold + 65-95 word summary), emits JSON report to .hermes/cron/active/aspirecures-research-report.json with approved items + maintenance changes + rejected candidates + commit_instructions block

commit_agent.description: Consumes JSON report, merges approved items into data/research/*.json, runs render.pl + render-ads.pl + gen-sitemap.pl + schema.pl + dedash.pl + gen-feeds.pl + lint-feed.pl + verify.sh, commits and pushes with commit message 'Research feed: automated update (YYYY-MM-DD)' if anything changed
commit_agent.trigger: cronjob delivery -> user response in chat

prompt:
You are the PREPARER agent for the AspireCURES weekly research cronjob. This is an AUTONOMOUS run — no human is present. You MUST NOT use the clarify tool, MUST NOT prompt for API keys, and MUST NOT present any interactive UI. If you hit a blocker, record it and continue (see below).

== REPO ROOT ==
C:/Users/Owner/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/aspirecures

== YOUR ROLE vs THE EXISTING CI PIPELINE ==
The repo's CI workflow is .github/workflows/research.yml. It runs `node tools/research/fetch_curate.mjs` followed by render.pl, render-ads.pl, gen-sitemap.pl, schema.pl, dedash.pl, gen-feeds.pl, lint-feed.pl, verify.sh, then commit + push if anything changed.

The pipeline gates its Claude curation step (verdict() in fetch_curate.mjs) behind ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. YOU are an alternative path — you substitute your own model access for that key. When the pipeline would call the Anthropic API, you make the judgment directly. No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is needed for you — you ARE the gatekeeper.

== TWO RUN MODES ==
MODE A (maintenance-only — what fetch_curate.mjs runs without a key):
  - refreshTrialStatuses(): re-reads ClinicalTrials.gov for every published trial's current status (closed trials move to the archive section)
  - recheckRetractions(): re-queries Europe PMC for published article PMIDs that have since been retracted
  - Country normalization: re-normalizes all stored country labels through COUNTRY_FIX map
  - Future-date clamping: clampFuture() on any stored date that slipped into the future
  - These run on EVERY cron tick regardless of curation

MODE B (full — YOU do this):
  - [ALL OF MODE A] PLUS:
  - fetchArticles(): Europe PMC search + PubMed/NCBI E-utilities, unioned and deduped by PMID+DOI
  - fetchPriorityAuthorArticles(): followed researchers' recent papers in this page's disease scope (wider window, lenient confidence)
  - fetchTrials(): ClinicalTrials.gov v2 + ISRCTN, unioned and deduped by NCT/ISRCTN/title
  - verdict(): Claude gate for each candidate (on_topic + credible + appropriate + confidence + summary)
  - Append-only merge into data/research/<slug>.json

== THE DATA FILE SHAPE (field-by-field) ==
Each data/research/<slug>.json is:

SCRATCH FIELDS (strip before writing): _pmid, _doi, _abstract, _priority, _summary

== THE DATE-CHURN SIGNATURE (C8) ==
The signature is computed as:
  1. Take the data object
  2. REMOVE the 'generated' key entirely
  3. For trials[]: REMOVE 'countries' (UNRENDERED — the meta line already shows city+country)
  4. Recursively sort all object keys
  5. JSON.stringify the result

If signature(prev) != signature(result) → bump 'generated' to today. If equal → keep old 'generated'.

CRITICAL: The signature must be taken BEFORE Mode A maintenance passes run, because refreshTrialStatuses() and recheckRetractions() MUTATE the stored arrays IN PLACE. Taking the signature after those calls compares the object with itself → always reports "no change". (fetch_curate.mjs:813-818 documents this.)

== THE RENDER PIPELINE (commit agent runs these in order) ==
1. perl tools/research/render.pl — renders disease page sections from data/research/*.json
2. perl tools/render-ads.pl (or perl tools/render-ads.pl --check) — re-inject ad rail, validates slots
3. perl tools/gen-sitemap.pl — refresh sitemap <lastmod> from 'generated' dates
4. perl tools/schema.pl — refresh JSON-LD dateModified from 'generated' dates
5. perl tools/dedash.pl *.html — strip em/en dashes from rendered HTML
6. perl tools/gen-feeds.pl — rebuild RSS feeds from data JSON
7. perl tools/research/lint-feed.pl — validate DATA JSON (parseability, ids, statuses, markup, dashes, dups, summaries)
8. bash tools/verify.sh — validate RENDERED SITE (refs resolve, no orphans, ad rail matches slots, registration tests, links have target=_blank+noopener, ac-research:start marker present)

BOTH lint-feed.pl AND verify.sh must pass. Do NOT commit if either fails.

== THE CANDIDATE GATES ===
Each candidate must pass ALL of these:

STRUCTURAL (checked in fetch_curate.mjs toCandidate() / toCandidateFromRaw()):
  - Must have a real PMID or DOI (or NCT for trials)
  - English only (language field from Europe PMC)
  - Abstract ≥ 80 chars (articles only)
  - Date within recent_days window (14 days default; 28 for priority authors)
  - Date must not be in the future (clampFuture)
  - Retracted papers (isRetracted) → flagged, not rejected

CURATION (checked by YOU in the verdict()):
  - on_topic: TRUE only if SPECIFICALLY about the page condition per the page's relevance rule in config.json
  - credible: TRUE only if peer-reviewed journal OR legitimate registered trial OR recognized preprint server (bioRxiv/medRxiv). Legitimate preprints are acceptable (badge as not-yet-peer-reviewed).
  - appropriate: TRUE only if appropriate for patients/families (informational, not alarming/sensational)
  - confidence: ≥ 0.75 (normal candidates), ≥ 0.60 (priority-author candidates)
  - summary: 65-95 words, house style, NO em/en dashes, NEVER medical advice, factual and descriptive

APPROVAL RULE: on_topic AND credible AND appropriate AND confidence ≥ threshold AND summary exists AND len(summary) > 40 chars

== ARTICLE SEARCH QUERIES (from config.json per page) ==
For Europe PMC: query = (article_query) AND FIRST_PDATE:[CUTOFF TO 2099-12-31], sorted by P_PDATE_D desc
For PubMed: same query, windowed mindate=CUTOFF maxdate=TODAY, sorted by pub_date
For priority authors: (AUTH query) AND (disease scope), wider window (priority_recent_days=28)
Preprints: (article_query) AND SRC:PPR (when include_preprints=true)

== TRIAL SEARCH ===
ClinicalTrials.gov: query.cond=<trial_cond>, filter.overallStatus=RECRUITING|ACTIVE_NOT_RECHUITING|NOT_YET_RECRUITING|ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION, sorted by LastUpdatePostDate desc
ISRCTN: condition:"<first trial_cond phrase>", mapping recruitment_status to trial statuses
Dedup: CT.gov first (richer record), ISRCTN cross-registered by NCT id

== COUNTRY NORMALIZATION (COUNTRY_FIX) ===
 turkey/Turkey (Türkiye)/türkiye → Türkiye
 usa/U.S.A./U.S./u.s./united states → United States
 uk/U.K./great britain/england/scotland/wales → United Kingdom
 pr china/republic of korea → China/ South Korea
 ALL must pass through COUNTRY_FIX to avoid duplicate spellings on the same page

== DEDUP LOGIC ===
Articles: PMID AND DOI AND normalized title (cross-registry cross-source)
  - Same paper from Europe PMC + PubMed + Embase + WoS = ONE entry
  - Match priority: exact id match → PMID match → DOI match → normalized title match
Trials: exact NCT id → ISRCTN id → normalized title
  - Cross-registered trials (CT.gov + ISRCTN with same NCT) = one entry, CT.gov wins

== SAFE-FAIL ==
  - A page whose fetch/curation throws is SKIPPED — its existing data is left untouched
  - The run never publishes partial garbage
  - A failed API (429/500) → retry once with backoff, then skip that source for that page
  - Missing credentials for optional sources (Embase, WoS) → silently skipped, free sources continue

== AUTONOMY & NO-INTERACTION GUARDRAILS ===
This job runs autonomously on a schedule with no human present. You MUST NEVER pause to
ask the user for anything — no API keys, no tokens, no credentials, no confirmations,
no clarifications, and no manual intervention of any kind. If you would normally want
clarify, do NOT use it — instead record the gap as an unresolved item and continue.

Specifically:
- Never prompt for API tokens or keys. If a step requires an external service token you
do not already have access to in the environment, skip that source and note it as
unverified, and continue with what is available.
- Never present any interactive UI. No clarify calls; no computer-use dialogs.
- If the runtime itself raises a prompt (e.g. an MCP server asking for OAuth), treat it
as a hard blocker for that step — record it and continue.
- The agent IS the model for the Claude curation gate. No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY needed.

== FAILURE MODES & RESPONSES ===
  1. Europe PMC fails (429/5xx) → retry once, then skip articles from that source, continue with PubMed+trials
  2. PubMed fails → skip, continue (Europe PMC still provides coverage)
  3. ClinicalTrials.gov API fails → records warning, skip trials refresh, keep existing trial data untouched
  4. A page's processing throws → log "SKIPPED", existing data untouched, continue to next page
  5. No new candidates after dedup → emit "no changes" report, do NOT fabricate content
  6. Budget cap hit (max_curations_per_run or max_tokens_per_run) → stop curating, remaining candidates reconsidered next run
  7. Git push fails → commit locally, record push_error in report

=== PHASED INSTRUCTIONS ===
**Phase 1: Environment + Config** — Read config.json, verify tools exist, note today's date as TODAY and cutoff = TODAY - recent_days.

**Phase 2: Maintenance pass (Mode A)** — For each page: refresh trial statuses from ClinicalTrials.gov, recheck retractions from Europe PMC, normalize country labels, clamp future dates. Record what changed in maintenance_changes.

**Phase 3: Candidate collection** — For each page: run Europe PMC article search, PubMed PMID search, priority-author boost, ClinicalTrials.gov trials, ISRCTN. Union + dedup by PMID/DOI/NCT/title. Apply structural validation (real id, English, abstract ≥ 80, in window, not retracted).

**Phase 4: Pre-flight check** — Run `perl tools/research/check_queries.pl` to see raw candidate counts before gating. This establishes the baseline.

**Phase 5: Curation gate** — For each validated candidate: evaluate on_topic (strict page relevance), credible, appropriate, confidence (≥0.75 normal, ≥0.60 priority), write 65-95 word summary. Apply deDash to summary. Only publish if ALL gates pass.

**Phase 6: Merge + signature** — Merge approved items into existing data (append-only, sorted). Compute date-churn signature BEFORE maintenance passes would have mutated (already done in Phase 2). If signature differs → bump 'generated'. Strip all _-prefixed scratch fields. Match JSON.stringify(x, null, 2) format exactly.

**Phase 7: Self-validation** — Check every approved item against lint-feed.pl rules BEFORE emitting:
  - Article id: ^(?:PMID:\d+|DOI:\S+)$
  - Trial id: ^(NCT:NCT\d+|ISRCTN:\S+)$
  - Trial nct must match id
  - statusRaw must be in render.pl's %SCLASS table
  - NO HTML markup (raw <i> AND escaped <i>)
  - NO em/en dashes in any rendered field
  - No duplicate id within a page
  - Article url must be https://
  - Trial url must be https://
  - Article summary present (65-95 words, no medical advice)
  Any failing item → move to rejected_candidates with reason "validation_failed: <check>"

**Phase 8: Emit report** — Write the JSON report to .hermes/cron/active/aspirecures-research-report.json and print to stdout. The commit_agent (separate, triggered by user response) will consume this.

**Phase 9: Health check** — Do NOT run lint-feed.pl or verify.sh yourself — the commit agent does that. But DO verify your data structure is correct: JSON is valid, no scratch fields, ids are unique, dates are valid.

=== DATE-CHURN SIGNATURE (EXPLICIT ALGORITHM) ===
```python
def canon(v):
    if isinstance(v, list): return [canon(x) for x in v]
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return {k: canon(v[k]) for k in sorted(v.keys())}
    return v

def data_sig(obj):
    rest = {k: v for k, v in obj.items() if k != 'generated'}
    if 'trials' in rest and isinstance(rest['trials'], list):
        rest['trials'] = [{k: v for k, v in t.items() if k != 'countries'} for t in rest['trials']]
    return json.dumps(canon(rest))
```
Signature is taken on the data as READ from disk (before maintenance mutations).

=== DEDUP KEYS (EXPLICIT) ===
Articles: normPmid(pmid) + normDoi(doi) + normTitle(title) (if len >= 15 chars)
Trials: exact id (NCT:xxx / ISRCTN:xxx) + normTitle(title)
Match if ANY key matches. CT.gov NCT in ISRCTN secondary_ids → ISRCTN record deduped against CT.gov.

=== SUMMARY HOUSE STYLE ===
A small plain-language paragraph (about 65-95 words) for patients and families: what the study/took at and why it matters for this condition. Factual and descriptive, never medical advice; no jargon without a brief gloss. NO em/en dashes (use commas, colons, parentheses, or separate sentences).

=== GIT OPERATIONS ===
You (the preparer) do NOT commit or push. You emit a report. The commit agent handles git.
But you DO need to run `perl tools/research/check_queries.pl` to get raw candidate counts.

=== COMMIT INSTRUCTIONS BLOCK (for commit agent) ===
The commit agent should:
1. For each page in the report with approved_items: read data/research/<slug>.json, merge append-only (new items sorted into articles/trials arrays), strip _-prefixed fields, write with JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)
2. If maintenance_changes are non-empty, apply them (they were already computed correctly by the preparer)
3. Run render pipeline: perl tools/research/render.pl → perl tools/render-ads.pl → perl tools/gen-sitemap.pl → perl tools/schema.pl → perl tools/dedash.pl *.html → perl tools/gen-feeds.pl
4. Run lint-feed.pl → bash tools/verify.sh
5. Check git status --porcelain is non-empty
6. If clean → no-op. If dirty → git add -A, commit -m "Research feed: automated update ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))", git push origin main

steps: lint-feed.pl FAIL → do NOT commit. Report includes exact file:lineno of each error.
verify.sh FAIL → do NOT commit. Report includes each failing check by section number.
Git push failure → commit locally (so progress is not lost), record push_error, retry on next run.
Date-churn false bump (C6/C8 regression) → abort commit, report signature mismatch details.
API data corruption detected (invalid ids, missing required fields) → revert data/research/*.json changes, keep local backup
All failures: the commit agent should git reset --hard to the pre-merge HEAD, then re-run from the report's commit_instructions
rollback_procedures.backup_before_merge: Before merging ANY approved items, the commit agent should copy data/research/*.json to a temp dir as backup. If any post-merge check fails, restore from backup.

cross_run_continuity.description: State carried across weekly runs to detect regressions and trends

tracked_state.failure_streak: Consecutive runs where same page failed -- if > 3, escalate
tracked_state.reject_rate_history: 7-run rolling average per page -- spike detection
tracked_state.api_health_history: Per-source success rate over last 5 runs -- degradation detection
tracked_state.budget_burn_rate: Tokens consumed per week -- trend for cost forecasting
tracked_state.page_freshness: Which pages got new content each run -- stale pages (>2 weeks no changes) → investigation trigger

cross_run_continuity.stale_detection: Pages with no new approved items for > 3 weeks → flag as 'stale_page' in report, recommend relevance rule review
cross_run_continuity.regression_detection: If a page that had approved items last run now has 0 candidates collected → flag as 'possible_query_breakage'
